methods.label: Substitute and verify the identity
methods.explanation:
A formula valid for every positive integer must work when \(n=1\). The sum is then \(1\), so
\[
\frac{(1+c)(2+k)}6=1.
\]
Among the listed pairs, only \(c=1\), \(k=1\) satisfies this condition.

To verify that this pair works for all positive integers, define
\[
F(n)=\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}6
\]
for nonnegative integers \(n\). We have \(F(0)=0\), and for \(n\geq1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
F(n)-F(n-1)
&=\frac n6\bigl((n+1)(2n+1)-(n-1)(2n-1)\bigr)\\
&=\frac n6(6n)=n^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Adding these differences from \(1\) through \(n\) cancels the intermediate terms, giving \(F(n)=1^2+2^2+\cdots+n^2\). Thus \(c=1\) and \(k=1\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
